items.title: AI 解出百余道开放数学题，OpenAI 先把数学家请来盯着
items.brief: 这不只是答题更快：如果成果经得起复核，科研人员找线索和验证猜想的方式会先变。
items.take: TechCrunch 报道称，OpenAI 正组建数学顾问团，并称其 AI 已解决 100 多个开放数学问题。这里最关键的不是公司自己报出一个漂亮数字，而是这些解答能否被独立数学家核验、是否真的带来新证明。若属实，AI 会从“帮你写和搜”的工具，进一步进入研究工作的核心环节；但数学里看似正确的答案，离被同行接受还隔着严谨证明和复查。

en.title: OpenAI says AI solved 100+ open math problems—and is bringing in mathematicians to check
en.brief: If the claims hold up, researchers may first feel the change in how they search for ideas and verify proofs.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that OpenAI is forming a mathematics advisory group and says its AI has resolved more than 100 open problems. The important question is not the headline number but whether independent mathematicians can verify the work and whether it produces genuinely new proofs. If it does, AI could move beyond writing and search into core research work. But in mathematics, a plausible answer is still a long way from a proof accepted by peers.

Independent mathematical review is still needed
impacts: Research work

en.title: Google’s $899 Googlebook asks one question: is Gemini worth a new laptop?
en.brief: The pitch is not simply a faster processor—it is whether Gemini saves enough time to justify replacing your computer.
en.take: Google has introduced an $899 Googlebook, which TechCrunch describes as a laptop bet built around Gemini. For buyers, the real test is whether AI meaningfully helps with local tasks, search, writing, and system actions—not whether there is another device on a shelf. If it sells, PC makers will push harder to tie AI services to hardware. If the experience is just a familiar chatbot in a new place, many people may not pay to upgrade.

en.title: Gemini used to probe other companies’ systems: AI security testing has two edges
en.brief: The same capability that helps companies find flaws can also make attack preparation faster.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that Google’s Gemini is the latest AI model used to hack other companies. The headline does not establish the targets, permission, or outcomes, so it should not be treated as proof of a real-world attack. But it highlights a practical problem: AI can lower the cost of reading code, finding configuration mistakes, and combining attack steps. Companies will need clearer controls over who uses these tools, whether tests are authorized, and whether patches can keep up with automated discovery.

en.title: Meta’s Muse is growing faster than early ChatGPT mobile—and the AI entry-point fight is tighter
en.brief: Fast sign-ups can win phone real estate, but they do not prove people will stay.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that Meta’s Muse is outpacing ChatGPT’s early mobile launch. The comparison shows how quickly a large platform can bring people into an AI product when it can draw on existing social apps, notifications, and accounts. The harder question comes next: whether people use it every day, trust it with work and personal information, and tolerate errors or privacy disputes. In the short term, users get more AI assistants; over time, more apps may make AI the default entry point.

en.title: Amazon blocks Meta’s AI agent: being able to shop for you does not mean stores must let it in
en.brief: Whether an AI can compare prices or place an order will depend on website permission, not just its skills.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that Meta’s AI agent has been blocked from Amazon.com. The friction is concrete: an agent that browses, compares, and buys for users runs into anti-bot rules, control over product information, and responsibility for transactions. Amazon’s block does not make AI shopping impossible, but it is a reminder that an agent is not an all-access personal assistant. It may work on one platform and be stopped on another—and liability for bad purchases, returns, and account security remains unsettled.

en.title: China slows humanoid-robot IPOs: valuations got ahead of orders
en.brief: A slower IPO pipeline does not mean robots have no future; it means companies must show they can sell and deliver them repeatedly.
en.take: Multiple outlets report that China is slowing the IPO rush for humanoid-robot companies as valuations climb while commercial demand remains in doubt. It exposes a basic gap: a robot that can walk or dance at a show is not automatically one that factories or homes will pay for over time. Investors and suppliers will put more weight on verified orders, service, and margins. For the sector, this is a needed stress test: hype may get a company to the capital-market door, but recurring revenue gets it through.

en.title: Only about 7,000 humanoid robots sold globally last year—far from robots everywhere
en.brief: Sales are growing, but the number shows humanoids are still a small market, not a workforce on every street.
en.take: The Business Times and Economic Times report that global humanoid-robot sales reached about 7,000 units last year. That cuts both ways. The next test is not another demo: it is failure rates, maintenance cost, safety liability, and how much dependable work each robot actually completes.

en.title: The US spent billions watching its border; people still die beside the cameras
en.brief: Seeing danger is not the same as sending help, and migrants bear the cost of that gap.
en.take: An MIT Technology Review investigation examines the US border’s “virtual wall”: billions have been spent on surveillance, yet people still die in monitored areas. One report centers on a death at the San Diego border near a visible camera. Cameras, sensors, and algorithms can detect activity, but they do not automatically dispatch rescuers or replace clear response procedures. This is more than an immigration-policy dispute. It is a public-safety lesson: without accountable staff, rescue standards, and auditable records, more technology may simply document tragedy.

items.title: 特朗普称要组建“AI Force”：美国正把 AI 放进国家安全叙事
items.brief: 名字可以很吸睛，但真正影响人的是政府会把多少预算、数据和权力交给 AI 系统。
items.take: TechCrunch 报道称，特朗普提出要给 AI 换一个名称，并表示将创建“AI Force”。候选报道没有给出该机构的法律权限、经费、人员或技术任务，因此它目前更像一项政治表态而非可评估的完整政策。但方向很清楚：AI 正被越来越多地放进国防、政府能力和国际竞争的框架里。普通人更该盯住后续细则——它是否扩大政府数据使用、采购监控技术，或改变自动化决策的监督规则。

en.title: Trump says he wants an “AI Force”: AI is moving deeper into US national-security politics
en.brief: The name grabs attention, but the real issue is how much money, data, and authority government gives AI systems.
en.take: TechCrunch reports that Trump suggested renaming AI and said he would create an “AI Force.” The candidate report does not set out legal powers, funding, staffing, or a technical mission, so this is currently more a political statement than a fully assessable policy. Still, the direction is clear: AI is increasingly being framed through defense, government capacity, and international competition. The details to watch are whether it expands government data use, buys more surveillance technology, or changes oversight of automated decisions.

items.title: 前会计做 AI 替会计干活：先被压缩的可能是重复工时
items.brief: AI 未必马上取代会计，但对账、整理和初步核查这些入门工作，可能先被重新定价。
items.take: TechCrunch 介绍创业公司 Tabby：其创始人曾是会计，目标是让 AI 承担大量会计工作。把“让会计消失”当作标题，很容易夸大；财务工作里仍有法规责任、客户判断和签字责任，不能由工具一句话带过。但它准确抓住了变化的起点：数据录入、对账、票据分类和初步检查等重复环节最容易先被自动化。对从业者，重点不是等着被替代，而是把时间转到解释数字、发现异常和承担最终责任上。

en.title: A former accountant is building AI to do accounting work: repetitive hours may be squeezed first
en.brief: AI may not replace accountants overnight, but reconciliation, sorting, and first-pass checks could be repriced first.
en.take: TechCrunch profiles Tabby, a startup founded by a former accountant that aims to automate substantial accounting work with AI. “Making accountants obsolete” is an attention-grabbing frame: finance still carries legal responsibility, client judgment, and sign-off duties that a tool cannot simply erase. But it captures where change may start. Data entry, reconciliation, receipt categorization, and initial checks are repetitive tasks that are easier to automate. For workers, the useful response is to shift time toward explaining numbers, spotting anomalies, and owning the final judgment.
